detail.title: Thermodynamic Scaling in Information Engines
detail.summary: Physical memory systems function as information engines, where thermodynamic costs arise from maintaining distinct, reliable memory states against environmental entropy. Stochastic thermodynamics provides a framework to evaluate these costs, revealing that retention time and state reliability are coupled to energy dissipation rates. Current system models indicate that trade-offs between system schedulability and data integrity necessitate periodic energy expenditure, effectively establishing a lower bound on the energetic cost of durable memory.
detail.reason: Synthesis of thermodynamic costs for memory retention and reliability is now supported by both stochastic theory and practical architectural system models.
